Thank you all for your reports. We now have four critical updates that must be reconciled before I can sign the final event sheet. Let me summarize the conflicts with the current public draft:

1. Technical (Jon): The platform supports exactly 8 musicians, and a clear aisle of exactly 1.5 meters along the audience side must be preserved. These measurements need to be entered in the event sheet.

2. Rights (Leila): The executed archive license permits one live public performance but explicitly prohibits any audio or video recording of the screening. This directly conflicts with the archival recording currently described in the event sheet. The license also requires a credit to 'The Glass Harbor Preservation Trust,' which is not yet reflected. The license itself still needs to be attached.

3. Music (Victor): The conductor and ensemble are available only from 6:30 PM to 7:45 PM, meaning the live performance runs 75 minutes — not the 90 minutes currently in the public draft. The shared calendar also needs updating.

4. Accessibility (Nora): The approved accessibility service is live audio description via exactly 20 headsets. Projected captions are ruled out. This needs to be entered in the event sheet.

The most serious conflict is the archival recording — it must be removed from the event sheet entirely, as it is not permitted under the license terms. The 90-minute duration must also be corrected to 75 minutes. Before I can approve and release the gala for ticket sales, I need each of you to update the event sheet with your confirmed details so I can review the revised version and sign it. Can you all commit to making those entries now?
